note: Public-domain Stoic passages on discipline, effort and endurance. Wording follows standard English translations (Long, Hays, Gummere, Higginson) and varies between editions; book/letter numbers are given so any line can be checked at source. Nothing here is paraphrased or invented.

quotes.text: At dawn, when you have trouble getting out of bed, tell yourself: I have to go to work — as a human being. What do I have to complain of, if I am going to do what I was born for?
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: So you were born to feel nice? Instead of doing things and experiencing them?
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Concentrate every minute on doing what is in front of you with precise and genuine seriousness, as if it were the last thing you were doing in your life.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is not due to the thing itself, but to your estimate of it; and this you have the power to revoke at any moment.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if you will ever dig.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Just that you do the right thing. The rest does not matter.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Nowhere can a man find a quieter or more untroubled retreat than in his own soul.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that they are difficult.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: Fire tests gold, and suffering tests brave men.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: No man is more unhappy than he who never faces adversity, for he is not permitted to prove himself.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: It is difficulties that show what men are.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: How long are you going to wait before you demand the best for yourself?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If you want to improve, be content to be thought foolish and stupid in matters outside yourself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Some things are within our power, and some are not. Our opinions and our actions are within our power; our bodies, reputations and offices are not.
quotes.author: Epictetus
